answers.answer: The standard 16 spaces give each player 12 ordinary turns (three in each of four seasons). Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.

Hosting order: rotate servants (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round event; resolve applicable monuments and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; cleanup by sending all used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, and the activity tile back to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the round marker.

Passing order: servants directly to Available Service; gentry in your discard to hand; resolve round event then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Any servant used for an ongoing effect is expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.

Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, when reputation is 6.1, so the PR6 activity and PR6 guests qualify even if four Service Help actions later lower actual reputation to 3.4. Each Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service. The end-of-step-2 reputation is used for screening.

Resolve every positive favour before any negative favour, with order otherwise chosen. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative-reputation favour first to avoid the loss; losses stop at 1.1, but positives must be resolved first. A money penalty must be fully payable: use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; borrow if short and able. If unable to fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity; Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments for £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments to move a servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments for a full refresh, once per turn for this special action. At minimum reputation 1.1, special actions cannot be taken. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.

Host the Butler’s Room Servant Hiring activity using an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, except underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no money fee. The used butler is expended and the room upgrades on first use. The upgraded room instead may recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; it cannot recruit unique servants.

A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that regular type is available.

The Butler’s Pantry is the only way to acquire an underbutler: take one from supply into Expended Service. Butler’s Room and Hire Servant VP cards cannot hire one. Normally it reaches Quarters at your next service rotation and Available Service at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service VP card can make it available sooner, and once in Quarters Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. The summary does not explicitly state whether an opponent can recruit an underbutler; its stated recruiting option is one common servant, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Pantry and Butler’s Room

answers.answer: Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You may not buy a duplicate tile you already own; reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.

When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A duplicate drawn is stacked on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn; duplicates share one space and its price. Qualifying Reserve tiles go directly to Reserve and another is drawn. If multiple spaces need filling, sort only newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves its space occupied, so no refill occurs.

After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and later PR1 draws there too. Largest Wine Cellar never goes to Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard in this source, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve; Refresh; Courtship and seasonal upkeep

answers.answer: At each courtship first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. In courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme category tile VP, including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. On a tie, each tied player draws a VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle discards together and bottom-deck them. Then open Reserve, fully refresh Market, reveal next theme to the right of prior themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance round marker.

Final courtship totals tile VP across all four revealed themes; a category shown twice counts twice, including negative VP. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Tie is broken by highest reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied, no Fairchild and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective. Players then get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible, then score.

End VP categories: all face-up improvement tile VP (including negative/unused); gentry VP in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200 rounded down; and printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Victory ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position does not break ties.

Normally receive five objectives at setup and two at round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase final retained count and do not create an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together before putting them face down on the bottom of the deck. Tile objectives require owning named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.

A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), or once after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used cards go to bottom of VP deck. Retained cards stay hidden with objectives and score printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and VP.

Normal activity tiles must flip to the rose/upgrade side after first use; once upgraded, they stay that side on later uses. Hybrids start with underlined icon up and flip after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite each host their front activity once then upgrade into monuments, which cannot host again and begin monument benefit on subsequent turns. For hybrids only the currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.

Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn in the ongoing-effects step, on hosting or passing, but not during courtship; newly purchased monuments first pay on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works in hosting step 2 or passing step 3: place one available servant on it to reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; that servant cannot serve the activity too and is expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Monuments; Servants’ Hall

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile, one casual guest from hand plus guest’s normal service; doubles all guest favours, positive and negative; upgrades and remains an activity. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand with normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest from deck to attend, with no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours, excludes negative ones from doubling; keep guest in discard at cleanup; upgrades into monument. Each has fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.

A random player gets first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and moving clockwise, each chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds Dowager Countess (fifth family card); Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.

Each player sets reputation to level 1, position 1, with stacked 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters (1 showing, Max at bottom); no 7/8 counters. Each gets a butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady. Of families, Ponsonby starts with £300; the others have no money (Cavendish has reputation bonus, York servant, Asquith extra card).
For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to box and unavailable this game.

Shuffle starter guests separately from casual deck and deal two starter guests to each player; shuffle every unused starter back into casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and follow normal casual rules.

For four players select one double-sided monument per player plus one, hence five. At most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze may be selected. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count toward this selection.

Opening Market is filled until it has six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less including no PR, excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Ineligible draws are set aside and returned to bag after filling. Stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles show upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids show underlined hybrid icon. Sort spaces by ascending printed sorting number beginning at £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.

Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, one reminder token per player above track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme for open courtship and keep revealed themes in order through game. Base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards are face up on Alderley Hall. Thus first theme is not hidden and old revealed themes remain in order.

At hosting rotation, a servant in Servants’ Quarters moves to Available Service, and one in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters; each advances one space, not twice. An unused Available servant stays available.

No. Village Fair reward is checked at event resolution before choosing an activity, and a not-yet-upgraded Private Study gives no reward at that step. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.

Round 6 event is resolved after service rotation and before ongoing effects/activity choice on a hosting turn; draw two objectives and keep both secret with your objectives. The passing procedure also resolves the round-track event, so passing players receive the event.
Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. Other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.

During Builders’ Holiday buy any number from current Market and/or Reserve as funds allow, finishing all purchases before sliding/refilling; use the unchanged market and existing prices. Once a tile has been bought on Builders’ Holiday, do not refresh between purchases with special action or VP card. Refill resulting empty spaces together after purchase. Market Purchase VP card follows Builders’ Holiday rules; the summary does not state that a VP-card Market Purchase is barred from refresh between its purchases, so that detail is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing; leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal rules and sort by number, then return the set-aside Market tiles to bag and mix. Set-aside tiles cannot reappear during that same refresh.

Each reputation symbol is one increment. Move clockwise to gain, anticlockwise to lose; crossing position 5 to 1 raises level, and 1 to 5 lowers level. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5 excess is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; actions may be taken before or mid reputation favour to make room.
Money held is public. Players may not give or receive money between them; never spend more than held. The money supply is unlimited, using proxies if needed.

The activity’s exact number and types of gentry must be met; no exceeding or falling short. Ladies require matching gender, casual guests require casual type, and family requires family members, so family cannot fill a two-ladies or two-casual requirement. Family has no PR and requires no personal service.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity: Invite gentry; Reputation screening

answers.answer: For an ordinary guest invite, favours that invite new guests draw from the indicated deck, reveal the guest to everyone, and add it to hand; such guests do not change the current activity’s attendees. For screening, draw stated number, choose stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.

Dismissal is optional, so no guest need be dismissed if none is unwanted. It may target an eligible guest in hand, current activity, or discard, including one drawn earlier by a favour. Family can never be dismissed. Put dismissed guest on bottom of matching guest deck; it is no longer yours, is not recovered on passing, and does not score.

Lord: £200. Lady: choose to screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer a choice; Dowager gives both.

The admirer condition is a male prestige guest attending the same activity. A male casual guest does not meet it; a female prestige guest does not; Charles Fairchild is a prestige guest but the summary does not specify his gender, so whether he qualifies is unsupported. In any case Young Lady draws one casual guest and additionally gains two reputation if condition is met.
answers.evidence: Base family card table; Fairchilds are prestige guests

answers.answer: Charles is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are not family cards: Fairchilds behave as prestige guests, and dismissal immunity is specifically for family, so they do not have family dismissal immunity.

Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and reduces your own reputation by one. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
Barn gives one reputation whenever you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives no reputation.

The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant from the Servants’ Quarters area in addition to Available Service, once per turn; after use it goes to Expended Service. This is distinct from Service Help (pay 3 reputation to move one Quarters servant to Available Service) and ordinary rotation (each servant advances one space).
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile; Service Help; Rotate service

answers.answer: Private Study’s front activity requires a butler and two family and has no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. You cannot host it repeatedly after upgrade; the upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds only, without staffing/hosting again.

Unupgraded Main Library: butler and two family, draw one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library: butler and three family, draw one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring.
Objective VP card: draw two objectives, keep one, put the other on bottom of objective deck. It adds one retained objective for final scoring.

Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, usable immediately, including servants in Expended Service. Service Help only moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service and cannot take directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit: Refresh Service; Service Help

answers.answer: Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, not an underbutler, into Expended Service. Since it is in Expended Service, it is not immediately available to provide service.

Refresh Guest returns one gentry of choice from your personal discard to hand, usable immediately. It cannot return family from elsewhere; family in discard is gentry and the summary says one gentry of choice, so a family card in discard may be returned. The card’s benefit moves it to hand; it is not thereby an attendee, and whether it can then be chosen for this activity depends on whether attendee choice has happened; the question specifies before choosing attendees, so it can be chosen to attend.

Basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary service VP gives 2 VP for every servant in employ, all types and locations. The separate ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.

Monuments objective gives 3 VP per monument and explicitly includes upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category objective counts tiles in specified category; monuments and hybrids count, and a hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.

Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory and either Main Library or North Library. They need only be owned at game end; use/upgrading is not required.

Prestige guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest. Every-three-guests objective scores 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests; family excluded, and incomplete groups score nothing. Prestige guests include a final Fairchild.

Base reputation objective gives 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. Wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level (levels 1–7 score 1/3/6/10/15/21/28), wheel position has no effect; reputation tie-breaks use level, not wheel position.

Base West Terrace requires three family and a butler; the front side invites one prestige guest. Upgraded side also optionally dismisses one to four guests and remains an activity tile. The summary does not state tile favour(s), nor clearly specify whether any different service/attendee requirements apply on the upgraded side beyond this; those requested details are unsupported. It does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Other base activity tiles; Improvements and ongoing effects

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you, are recovered to hand when passing, and score normally.

Reserve tiles are public and may be inspected at any time. The summary does not say whether a Reserve stack must be bought from the top or whether any tile in a stack may be selected; that part is unsupported.

You may choose to host an activity or pass; the summary does not require hosting when possible. If the chosen activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

A passing player can take the free Market refresh benefit and also use the Refresh Market special action once that turn, as refresh methods other than the special action do not use its limit. VP-card refreshes also have separate availability. The once-per-turn restriction is specifically on the 4-reputation Refresh Market special action; the summary permits special actions on your own turn including passing. It does not clearly say whether a player can use multiple Market Refresh VP cards in one turn, so that extra multiplicity is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Passing; Special actions; VP-card benefit: Market Refresh
